chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Raib, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: When the believer dies, the angels weep over him, and the depressions of the earth upon which he used to worship Allah, and the doors of the sky through which his deeds used to ascend; and a gap is made in Islam that nothing can fill, because the believers are the fortresses of Islam, like the fortresses of the city's wall.

key_terms.بِقَاعُ الْأَرْضِ: depressions or spots of the earth

ai.seo_question: What happens in the heavens and earth when a believer dies according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) illustrates the metaphysical impact of a believer's death, where the natural world and celestial realms mourn the loss of a devoted servant. The Imam employs the metaphor of 'fortresses' (husun) to highlight the believer's role as the structural integrity of the Islamic community, suggesting that their passing leaves a unique, unfillable void in the spiritual defense of the faith.
